contexts.text: Barbarians and enemies () = those who look solely to earthly and worldly things.
To pursue the enemies (), here, = to drive out the evils and falsities which were with goods and truths...
Who hath delivered thine enemies into thine hand () = victory.

Thy seed shall inherit the gate of thine enemies () = that charity and faith will succeed in the place where before there were evil and falsity... Enemies = evils and falsities, or, what is the same, those who are in evil and falsity. These are signified, in the internal sense of the Word, by enemies, and enemies.
Enemies, that is, evil Genii and Spirits...
Enemies becoming the head () = that evils reign.
To speak with the enemies in the gate () = not at all to fear evils and falsities, thus not to fear Hell.
Hence it is evident what is signified by the gate of the enemies, namely, Hell, that is, the infernals, who continually attack things good and true: their seat is with man in his natural mind...
Before they have been subordinated and subjected to good, they are called enemies, because they continually oppose.
Yet they are the most bitter enemies... of mankind.
Under Domestic, see these references. AC 10490:5.
They were the enemies of evil Spirits...

Thy hand in the neck of thine enemies () = that the infernal and diabolical crew will flee away at his presence. Enemies = the infernal and diabolical crew; for these are enemies in the spiritual sense... When an enemy flees, the hand of the victor is in his neck... A celestial Angel never fights, still less is his hand in the neck of his enemies, nor for his part does he consider anyone as an enemy; but... it is signified, that the infernals, who on their part are enemies, flee at his presence.

With Thy right hand Jehovah thou breakest in pieces the enemy () = the effect of omnipotence upon evils and the falsities thence, whose power is annihilated... An enemy = evils and falsities; for nothing else is meant in the spiritual sense by enemies, enemies, and haters. They are called enemies, enemies, and haters, not because the Lord is their enemy, or hates them, but because they are haters and enemies against the Divine.
The enemy said () = the thought of those who were in evils and thence falsities before the Advent of the Lord.
To strike the enemies with the horn () = to destroy falsities there by the power of the truth and good of faith.

I will act as an enemy to thine enemies () = that He averts all evils from which are falsities. To act as an enemy, when said of the Lord, = to avert. Enemies = the evils from which are falsities; for, in the spiritual sense, these are enemies to the goods from which are truths. The reason enemies = evils from which are falsities, is that by enemies are signified the falsities from evil. (See Enemy, at AC 9313.)

Until I set thine enemies a footstool to thy feet () = when the evils which are in the Hells and from the Hells are subjugated, and have been subjected to His Divine power... To have dominion in the midst of thine enemies () = which good has dominion over evils. Evils are enemies, because they are against the Divine, in special, against the Lord.
Victories over the Hells, which are the enemies who shall be clothed with shame ().
To account as an enemy for the sake of a garment () = to do evil to them on account of the truth which they think...
Enemies = the Hells; in general, evils and falsities. References.
The Hells are meant by the enemy over whom they should have power ().

By flight before enemies () is meant persecution by evils and falsities; for they who attribute things good and true to themselves cannot fight against the evils and falsities which are from Hell, and which, in the spiritual sense, are the enemies before whom there is flight, and from whom there is persecution.
They who rise up against or enemies = evils and the falsities thence; for, in the spiritual sense, these are the enemies who rise up against us. Illustrated.
This was represented by that nation conquering their enemies so long as they remained in the worship which was commanded them...
A thousand enemies do not endure there one ray of the light of Heaven...
a. They who are against them and their evils are accounted as... enemies...
Their mighty ones and the enemies () = the Hells; for all there hate the Lord.
Enemy... is predicated of good, and, in the opposite sense, of evil; whereas enemy... is predicated of truth, and, in the opposite sense, of falsity.
(Thus) it is allowable for anyone to defend his country and associates against invading enemies, even by means of wicked commanders; but it is not allowable to become an enemy without a cause.
Infernal marriages between those who are interiorly the most bitter enemies, but exteriorly the closest friends. Explained.
The enemy () = falsity from evil, and evil from falsity.
Evils and falsities are the enemies who shall be clothed with shame ().
Enemies () = evils; and enemies, falsities.
The enemy () = evil; and enemies, the falsities of evil. AE 357:24. AE 642.
Enemies () = evils.
Enemy () = evil; and enemy = falsity.
Enemies () = evils.
The enemy () = evil and falsity.
Enemies () = evils.
Enemies () = evils.
Our enemies () = evils.
The enemy who has consumed them () = evil and falsity.
Enemies () = those who are from Hell.
By enemies in the Word, are signified evils. AE 526:10.
Enemies () = those who are in evils.
Those who are against the truths and goods of the Church, and their falsities of evil, are meant in the Word by enemies.
The enemy () = the evil which is from Hell.
The enemy () = evil from Hell.
By enemies () are signified evils of life.
The enemy () = evil, in general the devil, that is, Hell from which is evil.
The enemy who has reproached Jehovah () = Hell and the evil thence.

In many places in the Word there are mentioned enemies, [and enemies, and by them are meant evils and falsities; by enemies, evils; and by enemies, falsities; (that is) spiritual enemies, and enemies. Illustrated.
The king's enemies () = those who are against truths, thus the Hells.
His enemies will I clothe with shame () = the subjugation of the Hells, and the dissipation of the evils thence.
The enemy () = Hell whence are evils and falsities.
To return from the land of the enemy () = to be led forth from Hell.

The enemy hath destroyed all things in the sanctuary () = that evil has destroyed the holy things of the Church. The enemies have roared in the midst of thy feast () = that falsities have destroyed all things of worship.
That they were to be destroyed by means of evils and falsities, is meant by I will give the king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies (). Here, enemies = those who are in evils...
The enemy () = Hell.
The enemies in the gate () = the falsities of evil which are from Hell.
The enemy () = the falsity of evil, and the Hell which is the source of it.

These statutes signify that the men of the Church... shall fight against their enemies, which are the Hells; and not they who are not as yet become men of the Church... (These words mean) that they should not prevail over their enemies, but their enemies over them; for they alone prevail over their spiritual enemies who are in truths from good, that is, those with whom truth is conjoined with good.
The enemy = the falsities which have destroyed the truths of the Church; and the enemy () = the evils which have destroyed the goods of the Church.
The enemy who hath prevailed () = evil from Hell, thus the evil of life.
Though they go into captivity before their enemies () = if they suffer evils to take possession of them.
From the gall of the revenges of the enemy () = from the wickedness and ferocity of the Hells... The enemy = Hell.
(Redemption) is deliverance from evils and falsities; which, being from Hell, are spiritual enemies; for they kill souls as natural enemies do bodies.
